title: Choreo
description: A choreographed camera times bodies and lens as one phrase of movement. The blocking is scored: steps, turns, and the support share a count, then the phrase ends.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The blocking is the music. Dance floors, musicals, and some fight halls need the camera to partner, not to report.
One phrase: a lift, a turn, a stop. Extra flourishes after the count read as a different shot.
It is the wrong tool for coverage. If you need an over-the-shoulder for a line, shoot the line.
Choreo that wanders off the dancers is a tour, not a duet.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Rehearse actors and camera as one system: steadicam, dolly, or jib, marks on the floor, a shared tempo. Height usually stays human.
Parallax of partners and set pieces should land on the beat. Prompt: Choreographed camera with [Subject], bodies and lens timed together, one phrase of movement, dance-floor blocking.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when a dance, a fight, or a walk is written as a single musical sentence. Do not use it to pretty-up a scene with no shared rhythm.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Steadicam is the vest that can carry the phrase; it is a platform, not the idea. A Oner is about duration, a long take that may or may not be danced.
Choreo can be short if the count is short.
SteadicamLong connecting moves through architecture. Neither handheld nor dolly.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: La La Land stages camera and dancers on one count. The Umbrellas of Cherbourg treats color, step, and lens as a shared phrase.
Use them as grammar for timed blocking.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a wandering steadicam. The tell: the camera keeps going after the bodies have finished the phrase.
The fix: one count, a shared stop, no extra travel.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Choreo in film?
Choreo is a camera that shares a count with the bodies: one phrase of movement, then a stop, as if the lens were a dance partner.
Choreo vs Steadicam
Steadicam is a stabilizer. Choreo is the idea that blocking and lens are timed together; it can ride a vest, a dolly, or a jib.
When should I use Choreo?
Use it for a dance, a fight, or a walk written as one musical sentence. Do not use it as default coverage.
How do I prompt Choreo for AI image or video?
Write bodies and lens on one phrase, then stop. Example: Choreographed camera with [Subject], bodies and lens timed together, one phrase of movement, dance-floor blocking.
